versions.changelog:
No changes to code or documentation in this release.  
- Updated --raw-html flag to return formatted html only, removing all scripts, and return whatever is in the body tag
- Version bump only.  
- No new features, bug fixes, or documentation updates detected.

Major update: Application detection and LLM-powered question-answering added.

- Added raw-html mode to return raw html instead of json in render mode. Best for token saving
- Removed 31 files, including tests, documentation, configs, and sample HTML.
- Core extraction remains deterministic DOM parsing with zero LLM/AI by default.
- Added `--detect` flag for deterministic application/page classification before rendering; skips parsing for CAPTCHAs, logins, closed jobs, etc.
- New optional `--answer-questions` flag uses an LLM to answer application/screening questions from a resume, but only runs on pages passing application detection.
- Enhanced documentation to clarify usage of new flags, application detection logic, and LLM integration (including setup and output schema details).

Initial release of render-url: a CLI tool for deterministic page rendering and structured content extraction

- Renders any URL using headless Chromium via Playwright, capturing post-JavaScript DOM.
- Extracts structured JSON including title, headings, links, images, meta, and visible text.
- Provides single-command (render-and-parse) and two-stage (render-url + parse-html) workflows.
- Extraction is pure DOM parsing—no AI, no interpretation, just structural data.
- Handles SPAs and JS-heavy sites where plain fetch would miss key content.
- One URL per run; robust handling of output files and errors.
